text: __NOTOC__ Highmountain Peak (or Highpeak) is a large mountain located in southern Highmountain. It is the highest point in the Broken Isles. The mountain's trails and outposts are maintained by the Skyhorn tribe. Only two settlements can be found on Highmountain Peak: Greystone, and the secluded Ironhorn Enclave.

The Inner Sanctum is where the Orb of Translocation leading to Undercity can be found. It is inside Sunfury Spire in Silvermoon, and is reached by a ramp in the main audience chamber. Travelers using the Orb of Translocation in the Ruins of Lordaeron above Undercity arrive on a floating platform in the Inner Sanctum, and enter Silvermoon City through the throne room.

Jaffe Cloudwalker is a Highmountain tauren flying kites with Mora Woodheart at a cliff southeast of Skyhorn in Highmountain. He also appears at Dazar'alor, flying kites with Mora. He is present in Zanchul during Talanji's coronation. He joins up with the Dragonscale Expedition and can be found, with Mora Cloudwalker, selling fishing supplies at the Wild Coast in the Waking Shores. He is seen flying a kite.

Juju (or Ju-Ju) is an object that is derived from a life force, a spiritual power, called E'ko and houses an unknown power source. The witch doctor Mau'ari is able to derive juju from E'ko, which is unfocused supernatural power. Bom'bay, a witch doctor in training, referred to the mucus of crabs and the venom of scorpions as jujus. Deathstalker Maltendis believed that Shadowpine troll priests used the unknown power source within Troll Juju to animate the dead. Some of the undead trolls and their living counterparts carry juju.

The Kelani Magi were the creators of the Enchanted Gemstones, said to hold the power to make constructs out of pure energy. When the Kelani fell to ruin, the Razormane quilboars were quick to scavenge and covet these beautiful and powerful objects. One such stone was retrieved by Cairne Bloodhoof in the Horde's search for the Oracle said to reside deep within the caverns within Stonetalon Peak, and used its powers to power an enchanted bridge deep within the ruins beneath the mountain.

The mountainous subcontinent of Khaz Modan is found on the Eastern Kingdoms, between Stormwind and Lordaeron. It is the home of the dwarves, led by the Council of Three Hammers. It means "Mountain of Khaz" in Dwarven, in honor of the titan shaper Khaz'goroth. In the World of Warcraft Manual, the continent of Khaz Modan is referred to as both Khaz Modan and Loch Modan. It is bordered by the continent of Azeroth to the south (and associated Kingdom of Stormwind), and Lordaeron to the north.

The enormous, crystalline palace city of Kil'jaeden is where the rulers of the Burning Legion dwelled. It is located on the ravaged world of Argus, within a city laid out according to complex geomantic rules. Its curved structures are reminiscent of draenei buildings, only far more intricate and beautiful. Outland's draenei town halls were hovels compared with the fantastic structures of this city. There were huge machines for focusing magic, which once provided peace, harmony, and health to an entire world. Now they created a cloud of fear and despair. Lessah Moonwater is a tauren archaeologist and adventurer found at Thunder Totem in Highmountain. She is a native of Thunder Bluff, come to Highmountain to study the local Highmountain tauren and the legend of Huln Highmountain. She has an apprentice named Luron.

Lunaclaw was a level 12 named moonkin that could be summoned using Cenarion Moondust in either Darkshore or the Barrens. Night elf druids could summon Lunaclaw at the Moonkin Stone in the moonkin caves, directly east of Auberdine in Darkshore. Tauren druids could summon Lunaclaw at the Moonkin Stone west of Camp Taurajo in the Barrens. When Lunaclaw is defeated, the druid can learn bear form from the Lunaclaw Spirit.

The mage (also called magus, magician or wizard) is a damage-dealing spell-caster that specializes in burst damage and area of effect spells. Mages are well known for their formidable damage output, as well as their range of crowd control abilities. Mages are also capable of performing a number of utility roles, from conjuring refreshments for their allies to teleporting or opening Portals to major cities. Their greatest power has always been their creativity at finding new and explosive ways to use their magic. Mages wear only cloth armor, but compensate for this with a range of armor spells, wreathing themselves in flame, frost or even arcane energies. Nonetheless, when fighting melee oppo

Mage abilities are abilities used by mages. Most abilities are shared between all specializations, while some are only specific to one (or two) specializations. Mage abilities use three schools of magic: Arcane, Fire, and Frost.

The Magical Preservation Society is a mage organization which seeks to study and protect magic on Azeroth. During their research, they may try to harness or even replicate magic in order to preserve it. The organization appears to be affiliated with the Alliance, as Arcanist Elleryn refused that one of her magical study subjects fall into the hands of the Horde. During the Fourth War, Arcanist Elleryn was present in front of the entrance to the Blood Font, below the titan pyramid Atul'Aman in Vol'dun. There, she wished to study the magical sethrak seal that blocked entry into the pyramid, but has to be protected by Alliance adventurers from Commander Grogash and his Horde Scouts.

Maldraxxi (or Necrolords) are the various types of undead that inhabit the eponymous realm of the Shadowlands known as Maldraxxus and make up the forces of the Necrolord Covenant and its loyal Undying Army. In Maldraxxus, the birthplace of necromantic magic among the necrolords, strength is rewarded and weakness cast aside. The souls of the ambitious and contentious are forged into an immortal army charged with the defense of the Shadowlands, with masters of the powers of death turning legions of ambitious souls into relentless immortal armies, and necrotic soldiers being forged by an eternity of war or are made from the bodies taken as spoils of war. The condition of a game character gaining mana points over time is referred to as mana regeneration. Mana regeneration is made up of two components: Combat regen and Spirit regen. Combat regen is listed in combat under the Spells category. Spirit regen can be viewed by mousing over your Spirit stat in the character menu. Out of combat, players will regenerate their full mana regen amount which is the combination of their Combat regen and Spirit regen. In combat, players will normally only regenerate their Combat Regen value, however healer specs have access to the Meditation passive which allows 50% of their Spirit Regen to continue in combat. A Mana Loom is a world object that was needed once in time to craft a Bolt of Imbued Netherweave cloth. It is no longer required as of patch 3.0.2. The mana looms have still not been removed from the game and can be found at the following locations: *Shattrath City: There are two located in the market area of Lower City. The first is positioned between the three Tailoring Specialist trainers, Nasmara Moonsong, Gidge Spellweaver and Eiin. There second is located near Eral, the General Goods vendor. Watch out, the vendor vomits when someone completes Of Thistleheads and Eggs..., which can interrupt your crafting. *Silvermoon City: In the Bazaar, at the Tailoring shop.

Menethil Harbor (men-a-thill) is a dwarven port town on the western shore of the Wetlands, on a small island. It has a boat that sails to Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh, on the continent of Kalimdor, and an icebreaker that goes to Valgarde in the Howling Fjord on the continent of Northrend. Within the city are many vendors; a First Aid trainer, the Deepwater Tavern, and a gryphon flight master. Besides the keep there is also a blacksmith and an inn. Menethil is a rough place that plays host to sailors, travelers, smugglers, and pirates. Except for the bridge, the only other ways of entering the town is by sea or by a secret underground path leading from the town to the mainland.

The Mennar Academy was an ancient Highborne academy, which was one of the first to study the arcane arts. They first discovered the potential of the magical energies seeping from the Well of Eternity. They were very cautious in its application of these new-found powers, so they didn't join Queen Azshara and her Highborne nobles. Refusing to fall back when the city fell, they stayed behind and erected magical barriers, turning their once quiet home into a fortress. Unable to hold out against a full frontal assault from the Burning Legion's vanguard, the Academy was destroyed during the War of the Ancients, but the inhabitants didn't die in vain. The Midnight Court is a large public square located in the eastern part of the Court of Stars in the nightborne city of Suramar. The majority of Suramar's nobility reside within the Midnight Court, which can be found in the most affluent area of the city. The Jeweled Estate, one of the largest and most ornate buildings in the city, dominates the northern section of the court. The location can be accessed via the Gilded Market in the west, which connects it to the rest of Suramar, and has access to Suramar Bay in the form of the Moonlit Landing to the south. The mogu are powerful, magical titan-forged who live in Pandaria. Proud, hateful, and powerful both physically and magically, the mogu are the foremost enemies of the pandaren. They have fought over the future of Pandaria since time immemorial. They were created by the Keepers during the ordering of Azeroth to shape and protect the land. An extension of Keeper Ra's will, they were agents of order, obedient and mighty. They would later be afflicted by the Curse of Flesh becoming mortal, eventually losing their way and valuing power and control above all else. Mooncloth is a magical cloth, imbued with the power of the Moonwells. It is said that the first recipe for mooncloth was scribed by Elune herself.

The Moon Guard (also spelled the Moonguard or simply the Guard) were an elite group of night elf sorcerers who served as protectors and peace-keepers in the ancient Kaldorei Empire, which dominated much of Ancient Kalimdor. The order was established long before even the War of the Ancients and its members included talented spell-casters who dedicated themselves to upholding the peace and security of the Kaldorei nation. Owing allegiance to no noble or lord, save for Queen Azshara herself, the Moon Guard played an active role in the War of the Ancients, operating from the city of Suramar. Mooncloth Tailoring is one of the Tailoring Specializations you are able to choose in Shattrath City. Mooncloth Specialization allows a tailor to create two Moonshroud or Primal Mooncloth, rather than just one. The specialization also grants access to specific tailoring recipes. Of the three cloth wearing classes (priest, mage, and warlock) specialization is geared more towards priests as it makes items with spirit and set bonuses to help healing.

__NOTOC__ The Moongraze resemble the talbuk of Draenor. Because of this resemblance, some of the refugee draenei who have crashed in the area of these beasts have begun to hunt them as a sort of rite of passage. Acteon, a hunter of Azure Watch, often sends young draenei adventurers to hunt the Moongraze in order to prove themselves ready for future tasks (see The Great Moongraze Hunt). The Moongraze seem unaffected by the crashed ship and its dangerous power crystals, unlike much of the natural wildlife of Azuremyst.

This item is gained when Arthas Menethil gets the first crystal during the undead mission of the same name by destroying an Altar of Kings.

Moonfang Snarlers are wolves that appear in the forest of western Darkmoon Island. They start appearing when it's time for Moonfang to make her appearance. Killing most all of them will cause a zone-wide announcement of Moonfang Dreadhowls appearing.

In the same way that the Holy Light, the light of Elune can be used to attack, heal, blind, protect, bless, purify, and resurrect someone. The priestesses of the Sisterhood of Elune are dedicated to the worship of the mother moon, and can be found throughout the world, ready to heal the war-weary Azeroth with her light. The Moonglade wildkin are a tribe of wildkin that inhabits Moonglade. They are training the next generation of wildkin in activities such as dancing, casting moonfire, and sleeping. Thus, each year they celebrate the Moonkin Festival, inviting adventures from all around Azeroth to teach them how wildkin develop. During these occasions, the festival would be threatened by an invasion of satyrs. With help of an adventurer, they would help a moonkin develop by feeding it, save one of their druids who was poisoned by them, and ultimately deal with their leader to save the festival.

Moonstalkers are saber cats found in Darkshore. A characteristic of the moonstalkers is the striped, black-colored fur. Their coloration attracts some hunters to tame them, as it is exclusive to the moonstalkers and the Blackwind Sabercats found in the mountains of Skettis. Shadowclaw, a rare mob moonstalker, is located in Withering Thicket, and is hostile towards the Horde during the Battle for Darkshore.

Moose, also known as elderhorns, are large, antlered herbivores found in Highmountain on the Broken Isles and Stormsong Valley in Kul Tiras. Though they may look like gentle giants, only a fool would underestimate their strength. The Great Northern Elderhorn is one of the heartiest of the species that inhabit the slopes of Highmountain, and can survive for months in freezing blizzards. The magical Grove Wardens are guardians of peaceful, primordial groves within the Emerald Dream. However, they were also some of the first to fall to the corrupting influence of the Emerald Nightmare. It historically ran between Rut'theran Village, at the foot of Teldrassil, and the port of Auberdine in Darkshore, before the latter's destruction at the time of the Cataclysm. During the Fourth War, the Moonspray was called into service once more. The ship transported Maiev Shadowsong, Shandris Feathermoon, and Sira Moonwarden from Stormwind City to Zoram Strand in Ashenvale as they followed the tracks of High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind heading to Darkshore. The Moonwell of Cleansing is a moonwell in Ashenvale located near the southwestern end of Falfarren River, east of Mystral Lake and west of Silverwing Outpost. It is connected to Silverwing Outpost by a bridge across Falfarren River, which, like the moonwell itself, is not marked on the world map. A Blink Dragon flies in a circle nearby. Southern Moonwell.jpg|Moonwell of Cleansing prior to the Cataclysm.

Mount Akher is a small mountain overlooking Neferset City in southern Uldum. The mountain is a strategic point, however, it's only lightly defended by the Neferset while their city is under attack by the Ramkahen. Ramkahen Ranger Captain and the Ramkahen Rangers await a hero to lead the assault up the mountain.

Murder Row (or Augur's Row) is a seedy walkway in Silvermoon City, located north of the Walk of Elders and south of the Court of the Sun. It is home to the city's rogue and warlock guilds, and houses one of the two entrances to the Silvermoon City Inn. The lighting of Murder Row has brightened considerably in patch 6.0.2.

Naga Royal Guards, as their name implies, serve as protection for important individuals. They are believed to be a magically-enhanced strain of Myrmidons. They helped both Illidan and Vashj in their efforts. Even though the Naga society is female dominated with mainly females studying magic, these creatures are by far the strongest units in the naga army possessing both immense physical and magical power. In-game, they are so powerful, they can be considered on par with hero units.

Neferset City Outskirts is, as the name implies, the outskirts of Neferset City in southern Uldum. It's from here the Ramkahen tol'vir have begun to assault the Neferset. High Commander Kamses commands the army while King Phaoris, ruler of the Ramkahen, oversees the assault. Neferset's immortal guardians defend the city, unable to be destroyed while Dark Pharaoh Tekahn remains alive. Salhet and his regiment have met up with the main forces here as well.

Nelara was a Sentinel stationed at Feathermoon Stronghold during the Cataclysm. During the naga attack in the wake of the Shattering, Nelara was ordered to bring the survivors of Feathermoon to higher ground; Feathermoon Stronghold's tower. Later when the naga, were trying to break into the tower, she was ordered to bring the survivors to the mainland, and to request aid from Thalanaar as soon as possible. Although unwilling to leave her general back on the island she did as ordered.

Nightblades are a faction within the night elves. They fought alongside the demigod Cenarius with the Shadowleaves, Moonhunters, and Starseekers against Grom Hellscream and the Warsong clan. With the help of Cenarius they destroyed three Warsong bases; the Moonhunters, the Starseekers and the Shadowleaves established themselves in the destroyed bases, from which they sent periodic attacks against the Warsong clan. However when Grom found the Chaos Well, he and his orcs drank from it and became chaos orcs. With their burst of power they attacked the night elves and killed Cenarius himself.

Nighthaven is the main settlement in the Moonglade. It is a primarily night elven village that is the home to the druids of the Cenarion Circle. The village is located on the shores of Lake Elune'ara. It features night elvish architecture, some of it with stone walls. It also has a pair of moonwells. Nighthaven's location is considered remote and the village is usually sequestered to outsiders. It caters mostly to druids, who have an ability to teleport here. Druids also have access to exclusive flight masters. Nordrassil, meaning the "Crown of the Heavens" in Darnassian, is the original World Tree of the night elves, located on the new Well of Eternity, atop Mount Hyjal, in the mountain's summit. It granted the elves immortality, and allowed the druids to enter the Emerald Dream with ease, until the Battle of Mount Hyjal, which severely wounded the tree and where the night elves lost its powers. Nordrassil's roots grow deep into the earth, spreading life-giving energy across the world. This is similar to what the first Well of Eternity did before it was destroyed. Of the Undercity is a title awarded to Horde players upon completing Exalted Champion of the Undercity, which requires the player attain status with the Undercity and earn the right to represent the Undercity in the Argent Tournament. Forsaken characters can obtain this title by completing The Valiant's Challenge (Horde). Characters of other Horde races must complete their version of The Valiant's Challenge, then complete A Valiant of the Undercity.

Oribos, the Eternal City (pronounced oh-ree-bus and also known as the Undying City) is a very ancient city located at the heart of the Shadowlands. All souls who enter the Shadowlands are first sent here to be judged by the Arbiter before being sent off to their appropriate afterlives. Constructed by the First Ones and predating all memory, the Eternal City serves as a nexus between the various domains of the Shadowlands and is a gathering point for power brokers, wheelers, dealers, and anima traders. Oribos is the central player hub of the Shadowlands. Oribos is the first destination of the departed. Oribos is the gateway to the afterlives of the Shadowlands, where souls begin their journey

Pallid Horrors were elite wights that periodically appeared during the Scourge Invasions in the Undercity and Stormwind City, Always Accompanied by Flameshockers, Going through rampages on the cities while killing city guards (including elite variants not seen anywhere in the game and guards from the starting zones). They were for lower-level characters so that they could continue to go about the city without worrying that a high-level elite undead would rain destruction upon them. In Stormwind, they were first spotted at the Cathedral of Light, While in the Undercity they were first spotted in the Sewers and Trade Quarter.

Panzerkin is a nickname for a Balance specced Druid in Moonkin Form with defense oriented gear. The name is a portmanteau of (the german word for tank) and Moonkin, so called because of the Moonkin's high armor value makes it a potential tank form, albeit probably not as good as a Feral bear. Panzerkin can also be used to more specifically refer to a Druid who is off-tanking or tanking in Moonkin form, which can be done with specialized gear and/or in certain circumstances. See Tank, "What is Panzerkin?", Thunja's guide to WOTLK Panzerkin Tanking, and "Lithanials' Guide to Moonkin Tanking v1.1" for more details (see External links below).

Portal: Undercity is a Horde-only mage ability that opens a portal for the mage's group. This ability's destination varies depending on what phase the user has Tirisfal Glades set to. If Tirisfal is in its phase, the portal goes to the Temple of the Damned in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity; if Tirisfal is in its phase, the user will find themselves on a hill northeast of the Ruins of Lordaeron, next to Zidormi. The phase can be changed by speaking to Zidormi.

.]] Power Words (often abbreviated PW: ) are special abilities used by Priests to protect and strengthen allies. There are two other types of Words: the Holy Word and the Shadow Word. When Prince Anduin and his father King Varian Wrynn were attacked by assassins during the Remembrance Day, the young priest spoke aloud the power words to use the powers of the Light.

Power Consoles are machines located within the Vault of Lights in the Halls of Origination during The Halls of Origination. They are initially found powering the Power Terminal: Defense Matrix, but can be routed to instead power the Power Terminal: Maker's Rise.

The Power Terminal: Maker's Rise is located within the Vault of Lights in the Halls of Origination during The Halls of Origination. Initially unpowered, the two Power Consoles found near the Power Terminal: Defense Matrix, will allow rerouting of the power, in order to get the lift moving again.

The Power Terminal: Defense Matrix is located within the Vault of Lights in the Halls of Origination during The Halls of Origination. This terminal is powered, but two nearby Power Consoles will allow the power to be routed to the Power Terminal: Maker's Rise instead.

The priest is the master of healing and preservation, restoring their wounded allies, shielding them in battle and even resurrecting their fallen comrades from death. Priests use powerful healing magic to fortify themselves and their allies. They also wield powerful offensive spells from a distance, but can be overwhelmed by enemies due to their physical frailty and minimal armor. Almost every class has some combination of abilities that unpredictably proc, buffs or debuffs of varying duration, and temporary haste-increasing abilities that alter cooldown length. The Ruins of Alterac (or Alterac Ruins) are what remains of the former Alterac City (or the Keep at Alterac) located in the Alterac Mountains. The city was the capital city of the Kingdom of Alterac, until it was attacked and put under martial law by King Terenas Menethil II and the Alliance of Lordaeron for their treason and pact with the Old Horde. Following the fall of the kingdom, the ruins became home to the Crushridge ogres who disputed the territories for years with the Syndicate. During the events of the Fourth War, the New Horde took over the ruins and began to build a major base here in order to keep power over the region. They were not contested by the Alliance, but were spied on.

The Ruins of Feathermoon are what remains of the old Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle off the coast of Feralas, after the attack of the Hatecrest naga during the Cataclysm. A new Feathermoon Stronghold was built on the mainland, while a number of Feathermoon's forces and Gilnean soldiers remained on the island to fight off the naga.

The Ruby Oathstone is the oathstone of the red dragonflight, located at on the southeastern side of the Ruby Lifeshrine in the Waking Shores. The symbol of the red dragonflight's calling to protect life, it once cast its glow high into the air for all to see. Alexstrasza believes that it and all of the other oathstones went dormant when she and the other Aspects sacrificed their powers to defeat Deathwing during the Cataclysm. The oathstone was restored when Sabellian returned the long-absent eggs of the black dragonflight to the Life Pools and thereby helped the red flight fulfill their calling.
Runic magic is a magic that employs runes/sigils, symbols that hold magical power. Types of magic that runes can access include light, void, fel, arcane, and death.

Sacrifice is an ability of the Voidwalker, a warlock minion. It consumes a portion of the Voidwalker's health, granting the warlock an absorption shield that is similar to a priest's Power Word: Shield ability. The ability consumes 25% of the voidwalker's base health, so as long as the voidwalker isn't near death, there is very little chance that the use of this ability will kill the demon. The duration of the Sacrifice shield is 30 seconds. Sacrifice is learned automatically by your Voidwalker at level 28.

The Sanctum of Order, built upon two of the city's levels, houses several notable features. In the Sanctum's lower levels, there are numerous magically-sealed cells which are used to house individuals detained by the Duskwatch. Selina Dourman is a Forsaken greeter located in the Darkmoon Faire on Darkmoon Island, which is only available during the monthly Darkmoon Faire event. She gives out information about the faire to curious adventurers. If you talk to her, she can give you a new Darkmoon Adventurer's Guide.

Though Ner'zhul had forsaken this tradition and his ancestors solely to save their people from 's wrath, the Shadowmoon Exile orcs nonetheless chose to leave. They assisted the draenei and the Alliance in undoing Ner'zhul's work, hoping to end his madness before it was too late. The Shadowmoon Exiles are led by Rulkan, Ner'zhul's ex-mate.

Shattered Sun Peacekeepers are draenei and blood elven guards aligned with the Shattered Sun Offensive who defend the town of Sun's Reach from hooligans, miscreants and those who try to start fights in town with the opposite faction. They leave the job of fighting off the Burning Legion demons, Dawnblade blood elves and other threats to the Shattered Sun Warriors and Shattered Sun Marksmen. These guards are swift and powerful and will strike down those who break the peace and unfortunately, even those who try to protect themselves by responding with a simple attack or defense mechanism.

Shatterspear Vale is a small valley surrounded by mountainous cliffs on all sides that houses a village inhabited by the trolls of the Shatterspear tribe in Darkshore in Kalimdor. Mountains and trees ring the vale, skimming the sky. For thousands of years, its waterfall beat against the ground, carving the bowl of the vale. The waterfall flows into a large pool whose shoreline is doted with Shatterspear huts and smaller fishing tents.

Shattering Blow was an ability granted to Feral Druids when they cast Symbiosis on a Warrior. It was a version of the Warrior ability Shattering Throw. This ability could be used to remove a Paladin's Divine Shield or a Mage's Ice Block.

The Shrine of Seven Stars is an ancient mogu structure located south of Mogu'shan Palace in the eastern part of the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. It has been claimed by the Alliance and serves as the main hub of the faction in the continent of Pandaria, as opposed to the sanctuary cities serving as main hubs for both factions in previous expansions. The Horde equivalent is the Shrine of Two Moons, found on the opposite side of Mogu'shan Palace. Within the Vale of Eternal Twilight, N'Zoth's twisted desire of the Vale of Eternal Blossoms made manifest, the Shrine of Seven Stars is the last remaining unconquered Shrine within the Vale, with the Shrine of Two Moons having fallen to the Black Empire.

The South Seas islands were two islands situated to the southeast of Land's End Beach in Tanaris. Until the release of Ahn'Qiraj, the islands were deserted and only had a Message in a Bottle on the southern island. The message read "What the heck are you dong here?". The bottle was removed in patch 1.8.0, though its shadow remained. The goblin and gnomish structures were added in patch 2.0.1. The islands were removed entirely from the game in patch 4.0.3a.

Starfall is an arcane spell available to druids, Priestess of the Moon, and possibly mages, priests, sorcerers, warlocks and wizards. The caster turns starlight into devastating missiles. The caster calls down starlight that solidifies into a destructive missile of matter and energy. The missiles appear as searing stars from the air above the targets, rocketing down into them with devastating explosive power. A caster is able to concentrate, and target two creatures, structures or objects with one starlight missile each that causes force damage. It can target different creatures, or the same creature repeatedly. However it cannot target the same creature with both missiles at the same time.

The area is now inhabited with Corrupted Sentinels. Brother Ravenoak has woken up, and appears to have been corrupted by the tendrils. Local cultures consider the mountain sacred. It is suffused by magic.

Telogrus Rift is the fragmented remains of an ancient, Void-infested world that was destroyed long ago by a powerful being, killing the "great ones" that inhabited it. This is where the void elves have taken residence, but unchecked Void energies ravage the floating islands, forming a growing Voidstorm that might one day even consume the big island entirely.

The Uncharted Island is a tropical island located somewhere in the Great Sea, serving as a tutorial scenario for Island Expeditions. There is an abandoned Kul Tiran fort on it, equipped with cannons and possessing a ship dock. The island is now occupied by hozen of the Kunzen tribe, and gorillas. During the Fourth War, members of the Alliance and the Horde arrived on the isle after reports indicated the presence of :Azerite on it. Led by either Flynn Fairwind or Captain Rez'okun, adventurers gathered the Azerite, which had been contaminating the wildlife. The hozen leader, Akakakoo, had also been collecting it.

Violet is a gigantic forest tallstrider and is one of many animals featured in the Darkmoon Faire zoo on Darkmoon Island. Violet's numerous offspring are usually butchered for food by Stamp Thunderhorn (such as Forest Strider Drumstick), but some are set aside to be purchased as Darkmoon Hatchlings for adventurers, and others are raised to become Swift Forest Strider mounts. Based on this information, the Darkmoon Striders are likely her offspring as well.

It is practiced primarily by troll shadow hunters, hexxers, and witch doctors as well as others. While not practiced by all trolls, voodoo is certainly at least as widespread as cannibalism. Little is known about its emergence among the trolls, since most tribes that possess such knowledge are unwilling to share it with outsiders. The Waking Shores are a zone on the Dragon Isles and the ancestral home of the red and black dragonflights. A wild, untamed land rife with elemental magic, the Waking Shores are the first zone that players see when they arrive to the Isles with a joint Explorers' League-Reliquary expedition. In the zone there are gorlocs. The zone storyline sees Alexstrasza summoning the Alliance and Horde to aid the red flight against the native Djaradin, while Wrathion seeks to reclaim the Obsidian Citadel of the black flight from enemy hands and come to terms with the state of his ruined flight.

Warder's Solace is a small island off the north-northeastern shore of the Forbidden Reach. The island is bordered by Dragonskull Island to the southeast and Froststone Peak to the south. Scavenging tarantulas control the island. Occasionally the battle pet world quest Shifting Ground takes place on the southwestern end of the island, tasking battlers to defeat Tremblor. Some Storm-Touched Slyvern are also present while the world quest is active.

The Whelping Downs are found in the Burning Steppes, south of Blackrock Mountain. Hordes of dragonflight whelpings are kept or raised here by the Blackrock clan. The Black dragonflight's whelps fly free, cared for and protected by Blackrock Whelpers. Whelps of other dragonflights are also held here before being transferred to Blackrock Spire, where they will be used in gruesome experiments.

Wildhammer Stronghold is an Alliance keep in the Shadowmoon Valley of Outland. As its name implies, it was founded by Kurdran Wildhammer, one of the survivors of the original Alliance Expedition, shortly before the destruction of Draenor. The stables of Wildhammer Stronghold are also one location of the Alliance's gryphon riding trainers and gryphon breeders for those seeking flying mounts. The dwarven keep was built over sacred, ancestral grounds to the orcish Shadowmoon clan, and the spirits of departed Shadowmoon orcs haunt the land. In , this same place could have been once home to Anguish Fortress and the Shadowmoon Burial Grounds, or Shaz'gul.

Frostwolf Envoys were orc Alterac Valley recruiters located at various spots throughout the largest Horde cities - Orgrimmar, Silvermoon City, Thunder Bluff, and Undercity, as well as the neutral Shattrath City and Dalaran. They were only available during the monthly Call to Arms: Alterac Valley.
Full Moon is a Balance druid ability, available after casting Half Moon (artifact trait). Casting it activates New Moon (artifact trait).

The Fruit of Fertility is a magical vine crafted many millennia ago by Millicent Serene as her crowning achievement. It is located in the Shrine of Eldretharr in Eldre'Thalas. Millicent used a specially prepared moonwell to grow the exotic and vibrant vine that was imbued with an aura of protection and growth. All of Eldre'Thalas flourished from its existence. The vine was falsely believed to be destroyed after The War of the Ancients. The vine was then found by Alzzin the Wildshaper and he corrupted it into the Felvine and used its power to enslave Ancients in his quest to corrupt the forests of Kalimdor, which earned him the name "the Wildshaper".
Fur Lining - Strength is a leatherworking-only permanent enchant to bracers to increase Strength by 57. It automatically changes rank at 500 skill (130 Strength), and 575 skill (500 Strength).

Galhara was a great night elven city some distance away, on the opposing side of the Well of Eternity, from Zin-Azshari. The city had hundreds of emerald crystals lining its boundaries. Amongst other things, these crystals in conjunction with each other could defend against magical attacks. It is unknown what happened to the city after the Great Sundering.

The Hall of Blood is the headquarters of the Blood Knight order, located within Farstriders' Square, in Silvermoon City. It houses the city's paladin trainers and Battlemasters. The Blood Knight Matriarch Lady Liadrin once resided in the chamber below, but has since been relocated to Shattrath City and more recently to the Sunwell. The Hall of Blood is opposite the main Farstrider practice ground, and two of the hall's denizens exchange dialogue alluding to the animosity between the two factions.

The Hall of Respite is the dwelling of the Blood Elf Magisters found in the Royal Exchange of Silvermoon City. Interconnected to the hall is the Silvermoon Jewelery. The hall appears to be some sort of relaxation "bar" (hence the name 'respite') where blood elves can satisfy their arcane magic addiction. Two fel crystals are seen floating above mats with teapots and cushions placed all over. A Blood Elf Magister can be seen periodically drawing energy from it.
Half Moon is a Balance druid ability, available after casting New Moon (artifact trait). Casting it activates Full Moon (artifact trait).

Heal was a priest healing ability. It covers the niche of a cheap heal that can be cast virtually forever. The downside is that it is slow to cast and not very powerful. For a far more powerful but less efficient healing spell, use Greater Heal (Classic). In situations where speed takes priority over mana efficiency, the quick but expensive Flash Heal may be preferred. While both these spells are undeniably more powerful, Heal is more mana efficient, and is a spell that can be used as a filler when nothing much else is going on.

Holy Power is a talent in the Holy tree which requires 25 points in Holy to max it. It increases the critical effect chance of your Holy spells. Many paladin abilities are unpredictable or ambiguous in regard to whether they use melee or spell mechanics. Generally, Retribution abilities will use melee mechanics, while Holy and Protection abilities will use spell mechanics. This talent affects spell crit mechanics.

Honor Guards are max level elite guards who serve as the personal guard of Chieftain Baine Bloodhoof in the tauren city of Thunder Bluff. They accompanied Baine to the Shrine of Two Moons and to Garrosh'ar Advance in Kun-Lai Summit on Pandaria. They were present during the feast for the Highmountain tauren. When the Void minions manifested in the city, they helped in its defense.

The Horde Emissaries are a group of ambassadors from each Horde race, they were sent as an envoy to inspect the new blood elf capital of Silvermoon and to ascertain their goals. guides them through the streets of Silvermoon. Due to the unusual political climate within the city, the envoys have yet to speak to an actual leader, much to the annoyance of Cheneta. The dialogue between the various emissaries ranges from offhand to intensely revealing from comments regarding the rebuilt city's decor to insight on the emissaries predicaments and reasons for being there.

House Stelleris is a major noble house based in the nightborne city of Suramar. Within nightborne aristocracy, House Stelleris occupies one of the highest positions, and stands as one of the most powerful of such factions within the city. Like most of Suramar's nobility, House Stelleris is based from the Noble District located around the Court of Stars. They are notorious for employing underhanded and cruel tactics to achieve their goals. House Stelleris has traditionally been allied with House Duskmere, and has been seen to stand against Houses Lunastre and Astravar. Following the Nightfallen rebellion and the death of its leader Coryn, it is unknown if House Stelleris still remains active.

Hrothgar's Landing is a small island located off the northern coast of Icecrown, in Northrend. The Sea Reaver's Run is the strait between Hrothgar's Landing and the continent. The adventurers who have risen in the ranks of the Argent Tournament, and were awarded with the title of by the Argent Crusade, were directed to the island with a new series of quests surrounding the kvaldir's taking of the island from the tuskarr.

The Icon of Argus is the racial icon of the draenei, and symbolizes their flight from Argus with the aid of the Naaru. The crest features a golden sigil that represents the :Gift of the Naaru and a number of purple gems connected by arcs of purple electricity, referring to their use of Naaru technology and skill with gem crafting. These rest atop a shattered shield, likely representing the shattering of Draenor, now known as Outland.

Improved Moonkin Form is a talent in the Druid's Balance tree, you will need to spend 34 points in Balance to max it. Improved Moonkin Form gives everyone in your party and/or raid 3% haste and grants you 30% of your Spirit as Spell Power while in Moonkin Form when maxed.

The infinite dragonflight (or simply the Infinites) is a dragonflight formed from corrupted members of the bronze dragonflight. Though it was believed their goal was seemingly to destroy the one true timeway and to bring about the Hour of Twilight, this was proven false. Their reasons for meddling in the timeways is to avoid, what they believe, to be worse fates. To this end, they pursue a corruption of the main timeline to one where they rule supreme, and control the dictation of events.
